verdicts.quote: “REST API authentication is handled through Adobe's Identity Management System (IMS) through standardized OAuth 2 protocols.”
verdicts.reason: Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service uses OAuth2; OAuth 1.0a/HMAC applies to PaaS/on‑prem. Per the rubric, prefer OAuth2 when a public OAuth flow exists.

verdicts.quote: “Prerequisites: Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service license”
verdicts.reason: Commerce SaaS APIs require a licensed instance; there is no universal free dev/sandbox for Commerce. (Magento Open Source is free but is a different product.)

verdicts.quote: “Adobe Commerce provides a wide range of REST API endpoints that allow you to perform actions on behalf of Commerce administrators, customers, and guest shoppers.”
verdicts.reason: Docs describe many resources and operations across the platform; breadth is broad (note SaaS has a subset, but overall scope is large).
Adobe publishes and maintains an official Commerce MCP server as part of its developer tools, contradicting “community.”

verdicts.quote: “Primarily the Cloud Service REST API differs in that it includes a smaller subset of endpoints.”
verdicts.reason: The API is well‑documented and buildable now, but you must handle dual auth models (OAuth2 for SaaS, OAuth1a for PaaS/on‑prem) and SaaS/PaaS endpoint differences.
